title: Tool proxy contract and observable fallback criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: downstream applications depend on deterministic structured responses and reliable tool/function invocation. When a model emits partial or malformed frames during streaming or when a tool bridge is slow/fails, caller services need a clear, observable, and testable fallback path. Goal: define an immutable contract for a tool-proxy layer + observable fallback behaviors so SDKs, Console, and Runtime can all react consistently (retry, degrade, surface error type, or route to fallback model variant).
background: We already have multiple PM specs dealing with streamed schemas and tool handoffs; this work focuses on the middle layer (tool proxy/gateway) responsibilities: conformance checks, canonical error classification, telemetry events, and safe fallbacks without leaking internal state. Recent customer incidents highlighted three gaps: 1) inconsistent error coding across SDKs, 2) missing telemetry for partial-frame reconciliation, 3) ad-hoc fallback logic in applications. This PRD aims to centralize the contract and acceptance criteria so engineering can implement a single, testable behavior across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
scope: Define the tool-proxy API surface (request/response envelope) with fields for schema-version, trace-id, and confidence metadata
Specify streaming invariants and a minimal framing for partial/continuation objects that the proxy will validate
Enumerate canonical error classes (validation_failure, tool_timeout, tool_error, transient_network, incompat_schema) and the proxy's default actions
Define telemetry & tracing events emitted by the proxy (names, payload shapes, sampling rules) and Console dashboard KPIs
Acceptance tests: unit, integration (mock tool), end-to-end with SDKs and curl, and chaos tests for transient failures
Rollout plan including feature flag gating, canary percentage, and automatic fallback thresholds
out_of_scope: Model-level generative corrections for malformed schema (e.g., model re-generation heuristics)
Custom per-customer tool adapters (these will be separate connectors)
Large-scale re-architecture of the retry subsystem unrelated to tool-proxy behavior
acceptance_criteria: Contract: The tool-proxy accepts a normalized envelope with fields: request_id, schema_version, trace_id, client_hint, and tool_mapping. Any request missing request_id or schema_version is rejected with validation_failure (400) and emits telemetry event 'tool.proxy.request.invalid'

Streaming: Partial frames must be wrapped with 'frame_type' in { 'partial', 'checkpoint', 'final' }. The proxy will buffer partial frames up to 4KB/stream and emit 'structured.emit.partial' for each checkpoint. If 'final' isn't received within configured window (default 2s) the proxy classifies the stream as 'incomplete_stream' and follows fallback rules

Fallback default behavior: on tool_timeout the proxy returns a structured error object shaped to the requested schema with 'fallback': true and 'reason': 'tool_timeout' and emits 'tool.proxy.fallback' telemetry. For high-confidence, low-latency routes the proxy will optionally route to a model-variant fallback specified in routing policy

Idempotency: Retries initiated by the proxy must be idempotent. Proxy will attach an 'idempotency_key' to retried tool requests and record 'tool.proxy.retry' with retry_count in telemetry. Acceptance tests assert no duplicated side-effects in mock tool adapter

Error classification: Each failure must be mappable to one of the canonical classes. SDKs and Console will display the mapped class and suggested remediation. Acceptance verifies UI shows the correct class for injected failures

Observability: Proxy emits the following core events: 'tool.proxy.request.start', 'tool.proxy.request.end', 'tool.proxy.retry', 'tool.proxy.fallback', 'structured.emit.partial', 'structured.emit.final', 'structured.emit.reconcile'. Each event includes timestamp, request_id, trace_id, latency_ms, and error_class when applicable

Backpressure & flow control: When downstream tool processing is saturated, proxy responds with HTTP 429 and emits 'tool.proxy.backpressure'. Configurable queue_depth and backpressure thresholds must be honored in Dedicated and Private modes

SDK behavior: SDKs will interpret the structured error fallback and surface a deterministic object to developers (fields: error_class, fallback, suggested_action). Unit tests across Python/Node clients must pass

E2E regression: Create a CI job that runs synthetic workloads simulating partial frames, tool timeouts, and transient TCP drops. Regression must pass with no uncaught exceptions and correct telemetry emitted
Security: For Private deployments proxy must respect KMS-provided keys for signing request envelopes. Acceptance requires a basic KMS integration smoke test
success_metrics: Reduction in customer-reported schema-mismatch incidents by >= 60% within two releases
>95% of failed tool calls are classified under a canonical error class and surfaced with a fallback object
Telemetry coverage: at least 90% of proxied requests emit both start and end events
Mean time to detect (MTTD) for incomplete streams decreases from current baseline by 50%
dependencies: ENG-5245 (SDK: structured error surface in Python/Node)
risks: Mismatch between proxy-surface and various SDK versions could cause developer confusion — mitigation: compatibility tests and clear semver guarantees
Introducing buffering increases memory pressure on the proxy during high-concurrency bursts — mitigation: conservative defaults and queue_depth limits
Fallback to model variants may change output semantics leading to customer confusion — mitigation: label fallbacks clearly in telemetry and UI
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal canary): deploy feature-flagged proxy to 5% of traffic in staging and run synthetic script for 48 hours
Phase 2 (customer canary): enable for 10 beta customers, monitor Console dashboard for errors and KPIs for one week
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): 20% -> 50% -> 100% over three weeks if KPI thresholds are met
Rollback: instant feature-flag removal and automatic route to prior behavior. Postmortem required if fallback rate > 5% after ramp
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope validation and error-class mapping
Integration tests with mock tool adapter injecting timeouts, partial frames, and malformed frames
E2E with SDKs verifying deterministic structured fallback objects and no uncaught exceptions
Chaos test: simulate 10% packet loss and assert proxy remains within memory/latency SLOs
Observability test: validate event pipeline contains required fields and Console charts render sample data
notes: Design has been discussed with Runtime and Observability on 2025-02-20; see meeting notes in Drive
Prefer a pragmatic initial schema_version 'v1' that can be extended; avoid complicated handshake for phase 1
PM request: keep fallback object minimal to avoid leaking internal tool error messages to customers
